correctness.rationale: For r>=2 sampled powers b^{e0}<...<b^{e_{r-1}}, the integer AP step divides b^{e0}(b^g-1), where g=gcd(e_i-e0). Thus index span >=(b^E-1)/(b^g-1)=sum_{t=0}^{E/g-1} b^{gt}>=sum_{t=0}^{r-2}b^t. Equalities r>=3 force g=1, consecutive exponents, first/last one at endpoints and maximal step, proving H, minimum length and rigidity. For three or more ones g is a proper divisor of E, so n-1>=b^{E-g} and g<=E/2 imply E<=2 floor(log_b(n-1)); the first two one indices and their exponent gap determine the entire sampled binary factor by the explicit rational formula, yielding the reported O_b(n^2 log n) counting bound. Boundary r=1,2, a=0 and composite bases are covered. Independently tested 2,352 exponent sets (126 minimizers) in bases 2..8 and 843,360 AP windows in bases 2,3,4,6 for lengths 1..12; finite checks do not prove infinite quantifiers.

The omitted boundary a=0 yields at most n additional length-n factors: if d divides some b^e, let e0 be least such exponent and j0=b^{e0}/d; its marked sample indices are exactly j0*b^k for k>=0, so the factor is determined by j0 in {1,...,n-1} or is all zero. Therefore P_w(n)<=P_c(n)+n=O_b(n^2), strictly stronger than the submitted O_b(n^2 log(n+1)).
